findings.summary: Hiding the inviter until acceptance means the invitee must consent to a connection without knowing who they are connecting with, which undercuts the 'two explicit consents' model and probably conflicts with any accept/redeem flow that shows the inviter's identity.
findings.evidence: "Invitation-based pairs formed by two explicit consents; the inviter stays anonymous until acceptance" / "an unaccepted invitation never reveals the inviter"

findings.summary: The anonymity rule is added as an effect of the owner's Invite interaction, but it governs what the recipient sees when opening or redeeming the invitation, and no redeem/accept operation is updated to carry it.
findings.evidence: effects: - Opening the invitation does not reveal who sent it until it has been accepted, so a forwarded code exposes nobody (on actor: ext.owner, trigger: Owner activates Invite)
